arxiv-2501-15611.title: Nuisance-free Ground Collision Avoidance Design with Adaptive Exponential Control Barrier Functions
arxiv-2501-15611.creator: Ege Ç. Altunkaya, İbrahim Özkol
arxiv-2501-15611.description: Abstract The significance of the automatic ground collision avoidance system (Auto-GCAS) has been proven by considering the fatal crashes that have occurred over decades. Even though extensive efforts have been put forth to address the ground collision avoidance in the literature, the notion of being nuisance-free has not been sufficiently addressed.

arxiv-2509-02062.title: Alignment of spiral and elliptical galaxies from Siena Galaxy Atlas with filaments
arxiv-2509-02062.creator: Yuvraj Muralichandran, Noam I. Libeskind, Elmo Tempel
arxiv-2509-02062.description: Abstract The properties of galaxies are known to have been influenced by the large-scale structures that they inhabit. Theory suggests that galaxies acquire angular momentum during the linear stage of structure formation, and hence predict alignments between the spin of halos and the nearby structures of the cosmic web.

arxiv-2510-13912.title: AI Debaters are More Persuasive when Arguing in Alignment with Their Own Beliefs
arxiv-2510-13912.creator: María Victoria Carro, Denise Alejandra Mester, Facundo Nieto, Oscar Agustín Stanchi, Guido Ernesto Bergman, Mario Alejandro Leiva, Eitan Sprejer, Luca Nicolás Forziati Gangi, Francisca Gauna Selasco, Juan Gustavo Corvalán, Gerardo I. Simari, María Vanina Martinez, [0.6em] FAIR, IALAB, Universidad de
arxiv-2510-13912.description: Abstract The core premise of AI debate as a scalable oversight technique is that it is harder to lie convincingly than to refute a lie , thereby enabling the judge to identify the correct position. Yet, existing debate experiments have relied on datasets with ground truth, where “lying” is reduced to defending an incorrect proposition.

arxiv-2511-03794.title: Primordial Dirac Leptogenesis
arxiv-2511-03794.creator: Aqeel Ahmed, Juan P. Garcés, Manfred Lindner
arxiv-2511-03794.description: Abstract We present a novel realization of Dirac leptogenesis based on the post-inflationary reheating phase of the early universe. An asymmetry generated within the scalar sector via CP-violating and out-of-equilibrium inflaton decays is transferred to chiral neutrinos through Yukawa interactions and then to baryons via electroweak sphalerons.

britannica-1911-macdonald-sir-john-alexa.title: Macdonald, Sir John Alexander (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-macdonald-sir-john-alexa.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-macdonald-sir-john-alexa.description: Article 'Macdonald, Sir John Alexander' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 17), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. premier of the dominion of Canada, was born in Glasgow on the 11th of January 1815, the third child of Hugh Macdonald (d. 1841), a native of Sutherlandshire. The family emigrated to Canada in 1820, settling first at Kingston, Ontario. At the age of fifteen Macdonald entered a law office; he was called to the bar in 1836, and began practice in Kingston, with immediate success.

pmc-11655274.title: Evaluating Active Learning Strategies for Automated Classification of Patient Safety Event Reports in Hospitals
pmc-11655274.creator: Shehnaz Islam, Myrtede Alfred, Dulaney Wilson, Eldan Cohen
pmc-11655274.description: Patient safety event (PSE) reports, which document incidents that compromise patient safety, are fundamental for improving healthcare quality. Accurate classification of these reports is crucial for analyzing trends, guiding interventions, and supporting organizational learning. However, this process is labor-intensive due to the high volume and complex taxonomy of reports.

pmc-12581295.title: Strengthening initial teacher education programs to deliver confident, effective, classroom-ready graduates: a feasibility study
pmc-12581295.creator: Nicholas Riley, Angus A. Leahy, Narelle Eather, Simone J. J. M. Verswijveren, Natalie Lander
pmc-12581295.description: BackgroundTransformEd is an evidence-based program that targets initial teacher education to equip future teachers with innovative strategies that increase the health, wellbeing and education outcomes of school children. Feasibility, effectiveness and implementation research demonstrate that TransformEd significantly enhances pre-service teachers’ confidence and competence to deliver such strategies. However, to date, the program has only been tested in undergraduate teaching degrees.

pmc-12985116.title: Understanding Australian Cat Caregiver Motivations and Reactions to Behaviour-Change Messaging on Cat Containment: Insights for Campaign Design
pmc-12985116.creator: Gemma C. Ma, Kiara L. Speedy, Patricia David, M. Carolyn Gates, Katherine E. Littlewood, Sarah Zito
pmc-12985116.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummaryKeeping pet cats safely at home is increasingly promoted in Australia to protect cats, wildlife, and communities, yet many cat caregivers are reluctant to change established outdoor routines. This study explored how people who allow their cats to roam think about their cats’ needs, safety, and overall wellbeing, and how they respond to different public messages about keeping cats at home.

pmc-13219728.title: Automated identification of MRI series using a hierarchical modular machine-learning pipeline
pmc-13219728.creator: Mariusz J Kujawa, Matías Fernández‑Patón, Leonor Cerdá Alberich, Diana Veiga-Canuto, Luis Martí‑Bonmatí
pmc-13219728.description: ObjectiveThe volume and diversity of large MR imaging datasets require efficient automated labelling tools for cataloguing MR series, as manual annotation is impractical and costly. However, relying on DICOM header fields alone is unreliable because sequence descriptors are heterogeneous and locally defined, frequently missing or incorrect, and may be altered or removed during anonymisation.

pmc-13454624.creator: Moonsoo Jang, Changhee Hwang, Soyoung Park
pmc-13454624.description: This study presents a data-efficient framework for applying deep learning to forensic shoeprint matching under realistic casework constraints. In forensic practice, deployment is often limited by scarce labeled data, distributional differences between reference collections and casework evidence, and a lack of practical guidance on model selection, augmentation, and adaptation.

pmc-13460223.title: TikTok, RedNote, and Bilibili as sources of medical information on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a cross-platform content analysis
pmc-13460223.creator: Yikun Cheng, Jian Ding, Qian Xue, Zegeng Li, Cheng Yang
pmc-13460223.description: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) poses a significant public health burden, particularly in China. This study mainly assessed the quality of clinical information and prevalent misinformation related to COPD-related short videos on TikTok, RedNote, and Bilibili.MethodsA cross-sectional observational study was conducted using videos collected on November 15, 2025.

pmc-13604797.title: Genome Analyses Support Global Effective Panmixia in Sperm Whales
pmc-13604797.creator: Muhammad Basil Ali, Menno J. de Jong, Ulfur Arnason, Biagio Violi, Céline Tardy, Filipe Alves, Marina Arregui, Rui Prieto, Pablo Covelo, Daniel Engelhaupt, A. Rus Hoelzel, Axel Janke
pmc-13604797.description: Simple SummaryGenomic analysis of 45 globally sampled sperm whales reveals an absence of global population structure except for a weak genetic discontinuity at the Strait of Gibraltar, making individuals in the North Atlantic more differentiated from conspecifics in the Mediterranean Sea than from conspecifics in the Indian and Pacific Ocean.
